title: Meet the three states
subtitle: A shape of its own, a shape that flows, or room to spread.

items.question: An ice cube keeps its shape on a plate. What state is it?
items.explanation: Ice is solid water. Its particles stay close and keep an ordered arrangement.

items.question: Water takes the shape of a cup. What makes it a liquid?
items.explanation: Liquid water flows. Its particles stay close but can move past one another.

title: A closer look
subtitle: Use a tiny-particle model to explain a big change.

items.question: Which description fits particles in liquid water?
options: Close together, moving past each other
items.explanation: In our simple model, liquid particles are close together and move past one another.

items.question: When liquid water becomes a gas, what happens to the water particles?
items.explanation: Water particles remain water. In the gas they spread farther apart. This drawing is a model, not a microscope.

title: Turn up the heat
subtitle: Explore what changes when water warms.

items.question: At ordinary air pressure, what happens to ice warmed above 0 degrees Celsius?
items.explanation: At ordinary pressure, ice melts near 0 degrees Celsius. The material is still water.

items.question: Water vapour touches a cold mirror. What can form?
options: Nothing, because the water is gone
items.explanation: Cooling can turn water vapour into liquid droplets. This change is called condensation.

items.question: Sugar is stirred into warm water and can no longer be seen. What happened?
items.explanation: The sugar dissolved in water. Dissolving and melting are different processes.

items.question: What is the name for liquid water changing into water vapour?
items.explanation: Evaporation is liquid water becoming water vapour. It can happen below boiling temperature.

title: Where did the puddle go?
subtitle: Follow water into the air and back again.

items.question: A puddle dries on a warm day without boiling. Where did much of its water go?
options: Into the air as water vapour
items.explanation: Water can evaporate below its boiling temperature. The water remains matter in the air.

items.question: A cool lid above warm water collects droplets. Which explanation fits?
items.explanation: Some water evaporated, then cooled on the lid and condensed into liquid droplets.
